title: OHLCV cache layer — non-blocking findings from PR #56's review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #56 (data-cache-followups-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. Both concern app/data/cache.py's `_upsert`.

checklist.step: _upsert's commit-time except clause was broadened from `except IntegrityError` to `except (IntegrityError, OperationalError)` to also catch SQLite's 'database is locked' outcome of the same concurrent first-time-population race. Unlike IntegrityError, whose scope is verified in an inline comment against the current schema (only the composite PK constraint on OHLCVCacheORM can raise it today), nothing verifies or documents that OperationalError can currently only arise here from SQLite lock contention on this specific commit. A different OperationalError cause (e.g. a missing table from a skipped/failed migration, a corrupted database file, a disk-full condition) would now also be silently logged-and-swallowed as though it were the benign concurrent-population race, rather than surfaced as the distinct bug it'd actually be. Not a live bug today (this code path only ever writes to an already-migrated OHLCVCacheORM table in the app's normal lifecycle), but worth the same kind of scope note the IntegrityError branch already has, or narrowing by inspecting the exception's message/args for the specific SQLite 'database is locked' text before treating it as the benign race.

The regression test added for the duplicate-date-within-frame fix (TestUpsertDuplicateDateWithinFrame.test_two_rows_for_the_same_date_in_one_frame_are_deduped_not_raised) exercises exactly 2 duplicate rows sharing one date. The underlying fix (`existing_by_date[bar_date] = existing` updated in-loop) generalizes to N duplicates by construction, and this was manually verified during PR #56's review with a 4-row frame (3 rows sharing one date, a 4th on a distinct date): exactly 2 persisted rows, the shared-date row holding the last occurrence's values, 0 IntegrityError -- so this is not a live bug, only a test-coverage completeness gap on the exact area the fix was meant to harden. Worth extending the existing test (or adding a sibling one) with 3+ duplicate dates in a single frame to pin the stronger behavior the fix's own docstring already describes generally, rather than relying on a reviewer's manual, unrecorded reproduction.

decisions.decision: Kept the OperationalError catch broad (still `except (IntegrityError, OperationalError)`, no `str(exc)`/`orig` pattern-matching for 'database is locked') and instead (1) added an inline comment documenting that OperationalError's scope is unverified/wider than IntegrityError's -- it can also mean a missing table, a corrupted DB file, or disk-full, none of which are benign -- and (2) changed the except-branch's `logger.warning` to include the caught exception's type and message (`type(exc).__name__`, `exc`), not just the ticker/interval as before.
decisions.rationale: The task explicitly offered a choice between narrowing by inspecting the error message/args vs. a clarifying comment/log message. Message/args inspection was rejected: the adjacent IntegrityError branch already explicitly rejects the equivalent move (parsing `orig` for which constraint fired) as fragile across SQLite versions/drivers, and 'database is locked' is exactly that kind of driver-specific string -- narrowing on it would swap one undocumented assumption for a differently fragile one, and this is explicitly 'not a live bug today'. Logging the exception content instead costs nothing at runtime, doesn't change any behavior/control flow (so no new test scenarios to cover), and directly serves the stated goal ('surfaced ... to an operator') -- an operator grepping logs for this warning can now see a literal 'database is locked' vs. something else (e.g. 'no such table') and escalate accordingly, even though the code path still treats both as the same benign race today.

decisions.decision: Extended TestUpsertDuplicateDateWithinFrame with a new sibling test (test_three_plus_duplicate_dates_in_one_frame_dedupe_to_the_last_occurrence) reusing the exact 4-row shape (3 rows sharing one date, 1 on a distinct date) manually verified during PR #56's review, rather than editing the existing 2-row test in place.
decisions.rationale: Keeping the original 2-row test intact preserves that exact regression case (the minimal duplicate-pair scenario the fix was originally written against) while the new test independently pins the N>2 generalization the checklist item calls out -- losing either coverage shape to the other wasn't worth it when both are cheap to keep. The 4-row shape (not just e.g. 3 identical dates) was chosen specifically because it also asserts that a distinct-date row alongside the duplicates is unaffected, matching what was actually manually verified rather than a narrower case.
